extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and intellectual property professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation and presentation of global design IP statistics (applications, registrations, pendency, examination outcomes, sectoral and origin/office breakdowns) and related normalization/definitions for cross-office comparison. Intended to guide analysis and policy using WIPO design indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, for a design to be eligible for protection, it typically needs to meet certain criteria such as being new, original and of an individual character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices perform substantive examinations for these criteria (checking novelty/originality against the register); other offices may register without substantive examination. This affects cross-office comparability of counts and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures (scope/variation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination procedures vary widely between offices: at some offices no search is made and no substantive examination is carried out prior to registration, while at other offices a substantive examination is conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because procedures differ, comparing outcomes (e.g., registration rates) across offices is difficult. WIPO compiles examination outcome data based on common definitions where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcome categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Design examination outcomes are reported in categories such as registered (approved), rejected, and withdrawals/abandonments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported examples: EUIPO registered 98.5% of processed applications in 2024; some offices had high rejection rates (e.g., Iran 57.8%, US 28%). Withdrawals/abandonments can be a substantial portion of decisions in some offices (e.g., Thailand 35.1%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially pending applications (definition/count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potentially pending applications are taken to be all design applications, at any stage in the process, awaiting a final decision by an office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices report counts of such potentially pending applications; e.g., US reported 76,665 in 2024, Korea 18,991, India 11,434. Some large offices (EUIPO, UK, Germany, Türkiye) reported relatively small pending counts relative to filing volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency times: filing to first office action and to final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Average pendency times measure the time from filing date to first office action and from filing to final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency varies widely: EUIPO processed in under four days on average in 2024; US and Thailand had much longer averages (619 and 720 days respectively). The gap between first action and final decision can be under a day in some offices (Madagascar, Peru, UAE) and over 300 days in others (Bangladesh, Cuba, Thailand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing time (average processing time following filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time taken by an office to process an application after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare office efficiency; extreme examples illustrate variance (EUIPO under four days vs US/Thailand hundreds of days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average registration age
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age of all active design registrations (time since registration) at an office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differs greatly by office (e.g., Spain 11.2 years vs UK 3 years in 2024) and informs survival/cohort analyses and renewal behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design registrations in force (counts and trend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of design registrations in force (total active registrations) and trends over time (2014–2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO reports worldwide totals and trends, with growth rates and office-level breakdowns (C29, C30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force as percentage of total registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of registrations in force in a given year expressed as a percentage of total registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess retention/maintenance; presented for offices (C31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts (definitions and counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of applications and application design counts (designs contained within applications) reported annually (trends 2010–2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note distinction between 'applications filed' and 'designs contained within applications' (design count). Data coverage caveats (e.g., China’s post-2017 counting rules) affect trend interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration design counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of registrations and number of designs contained in registrations (registration design counts) reported annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided for worldwide totals and by office (C4, C5, C13, C14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident application/registration shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of application and registration counts into resident and non-resident shares (percentages) and their contribution to growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show resident share (%), non-resident share (%) and contribution to year-on-year growth (e.g., C3, C10, C12). Examples: non-resident share and contributions vary substantially across offices and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth rate (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-on-year growth rate (%) for applications, application design counts, registrations, and registration design counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported alongside absolute counts to show trends; growth rates can be positive or negative and are broken down by region/office/origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts by office and by origin (ranked/top20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and rankings of application design counts by office (top 20 offices) and by origin (top 20 origins) for a given year (2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify leading offices and origins; includes resident/non-resident breakdowns and non-resident share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident filing route: direct vs via the Hague System
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between non-resident filings made directly at offices and those made via the Hague System, with Hague share (%) reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend series (2010–2024) show shares and counts for each route (C15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application design counts (regional office conversions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalence adjustment where an application filed at a regional office can be considered equivalent to multiple applications in the member states of that office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO reports 'equivalent application' counts to allow better comparison between single-country and regional filings (C20). See glossary for definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flows of application design counts abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic flows showing where applications from top origins are filed abroad (flows to top offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to map international filing behavior (C21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts by Locarno class
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of application design counts across Locarno classes (top 10 classes in 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for technical/sectoral analysis (C22). See annex for class numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts by industry sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of Locarno classes into industry sectors (12 sectors via OECD concordance) and counts by sector (C23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to present sectoral composition (e.g., furniture, textiles, tools); conversion method noted in annex C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of application design counts by top three sectors for offices/origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage distribution showing the top three industry sectors contributing to application design counts for selected offices or origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts show top three sectors per office/origin (C24, C25) to highlight sectoral specialization. Data availability limits noted for some large offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application design count per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalization metric: resident application design count per USD 100 billion of GDP for selected origins (2014 and 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables comparisons of design activity relative to economic size; GDP data in constant 2021 US PPP dollars; selection based on data availability (C26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application design count per million population
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalization metric: resident application design count per million population for selected origins (2014 and 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare design activity relative to population size (C27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application design count per capita vs GDP per capita
rubrics_metrics.description: Scatter/relationship between resident application design count per capita and GDP per capita for selected origins (2020–2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows correlation between economic development and design activity; uses PPP GDP per capita (constant 2021 USD) and log scale for GDP per capita (C28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort survival / registration longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of active design registrations by year of registration (cohort analysis) showing what share of registrations from a given year remain in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., more than one-quarter of designs registered in 2006 were still in force in 2024; most of 2015 cohort likewise remained active; >80% of 2020 cohort still valid in 2024 (figure C31 referencing cohorts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of design examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of design examiners at selected offices (C36).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of office capacity; reported alongside procedural metrics to interpret processing times and examination intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage, definitions and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on data coverage (number of offices covered), definitions (e.g., design count, equivalent application) and known comparability issues (e.g., China’s post-2017 application counting rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering specified numbers of IP offices; some large offices’ data may be incomplete or not comparable across years. See glossary and annex for definitions and conversion methods.
